svg.title: Pressure valves – direct and pilot relief, reducing, counterbalance sections (example)
svg.text: Pressure control valves – simplified sections: direct relief · pilot-operated relief · reducing valve · counterbalance
Light red = pressure that the valve controls. Every pressure valve compares an oil force (p · A) with a spring force F. ISO symbol in each panel.
to rated flow (pressure rises with Q).
31.5 MPa: use the lowest that fits.
Small pilot flow 0.5–1.5 L/min via the orifice;
Δp across it lifts the main poppet.
Vent X to tank = unload (0.2–0.5 MPa).
e.g. Rexroth DB / DBW, Sun RPEC (check)
outlet pressure on the spool end (feedback)
p_A rises → spool moves right → P→A closes. If p_A goes above the setting (load pushes,
heat) the spool moves further → A→T opens (relieving). Clamps need this 3-way type.
Opens when p_load + ratio · p_pilot ≥ p_set (seat area = 1)
Guide-25 job: p_load = 20 000 N / 31.2 cm² = 6.41 MPa → p_set ≥ 1.3 · 6.41 → 8.5 MPa
Free flow into the cylinder through the built-in check (0.1–0.35 MPa).
Rule (guide 29 §19): all valves rated ≥ the relief setting; counterbalance and pilot-operated checks go directly ON the cylinder port (no hose between).
Data from guide 29 §8.1, 8.2, 8.4, 8.6. Settings are examples – take spring ranges and curves from the datasheet.
